From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Simmons <jared.simmons@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-17T20:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today — Acme TCO recap & next steps

Jared — great to connect. Short recap below (TL;DR at top, details after). I attached a simple pricing model and a mutual action plan.

TL;DR:
- Estimated base TCO (annual) for current chat volume: $150k. With batching + 4x KV cache hit rate we estimate net cost ~ $85k/year.
- Short pilot recommended: 6 weeks, ~10k daily requests, objective: validate 4x effective batching + latency SLO (p95 < 300ms).
- Next steps: pricing deep-dive + procurement touchpoint. I can join a call with Priya and your procurement team.

Detailed notes from today’s discovery:
1) Volume & pattern
- You mentioned ~3M messages/month; 90% under 60 tokens produced, 10% long form (avg 600 tokens).
- Peak concurrency: ~450 concurrent sessions during business hours.

2) Pain points & goals
- Cost is the primary constraint (target ~$120k/year).
- Latency spikes during peak hours cause support SLA misses — target p95 < 300ms.
- Data residency not urgent for now (US only).

3) Recommended TCO levers we discussed
- Batching: grouping short requests reduces per-token overhead. For your workload, our benchmark shows 2.5–4x token-cost improvement when moving from single-request to targeted batching with your concurrency profile.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeat prompts (customer intents, system prompts), KV cache reduces decode work for repeated prefixes; expect another ~20–40% token-cost reduction when cache hit rate reaches 40–60%.
- Quantization/Model choice: Model variants (fp16, int8/4) — tradeoffs between latency and slight quality delta. For short chat paths we recommend an int8 variant that yields ~30% cost reduction on GPU with minimal quality impact.
- Smart routing: route low-latency/low-cost requests to cheaper instances or smaller model variants. Can be automated by Redwood to meet p95 targets.

4) Rough token economics (ballpark) — please treat as directional:
- Current avg tokens per short convo: 180 tokens total (prompt+response). Long convo avg: 1,200 tokens.
- Weighted avg token per convo: ~270 tokens.
- Hosted Redwood list price (example model): $0.0006 per 1k tokens (baseline). With batching + quantization, effective per-1k-token cost can fall to ~$0.00018–$0.00025.
- For 3M messages/month (270 tokens/convo): baseline annualized ~ $150k; optimized (batching + cache + quantization) ~ $68k–$95k/year depending on hit rates and model mix.

5) Risks & assumptions
- Assumes 40–60% KV cache hit on repeat prefixes and safe batching patterns for short chats.
- Assumes ability to route long-form calls to larger model variants without inflating baseline.

Proposed next steps
- Pricing deep-dive (30–45m) with Rafael + Ben to walk the attached pricing model (this week).
- Pilot proposal: 6-week pilot (MVP integration + load tests + ROI report). Mutual action plan attached.
- Procurement touchpoint: Priya to introduce procurement; I’ll share procurement/contract timeline and an initial SOW.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-model.xlsx, acme-mutual-action-plan.pdf

Happy to adjust assumptions — want to make sure we meet your $120k/year goal while keeping p95 latency under 300ms. Proposed times for a pricing call: 2027-04-19 10:00-11:00 PDT, 2027-04-19 14:00-15:00 PDT, or 2027-04-20 09:00-10:00 PDT. Which works best?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
